label: Multichannel Room (MC), AIS section, Aalborg University
note: ITU-R BS.1116-1 room; T20 0.29 s (50-630 Hz third-octave average, Documentation.pdf Table 2); IRs cover 15-600 Hz only (1.2 kHz): only the 63, 125 and 250 Hz octaves are analysed, rt_broadband covers about 45-540 Hz, and drr_db and mixing_time_ms mean little; 8 subwoofers, six near the walls and two next to the sampled areas (source 0-7 = loudspeaker 1-8); receiver A<area>_P<position>_<array height cm>, a 3 x 5 microphone grid 10 cm apart (mic_k = microphone k+1); condition = sweep length and silence. From the published 15 s IRs, the third-octave T20 averaged over 50-500 Hz is 0.30 s here and 0.56 s in the Listening Room, as Table 2 states; the long 63 Hz octave value (T30 about 0.8 s) comes from the 50 Hz third octave. The 36, 50 and 100 ms sweep IRs carry a known defect, and the 200 ms ones (0.19 s long) match the 15 s IRs at 250 Hz but end before the 63 and 125 Hz decays are done (no T30 there; T20 at 125 Hz about 15 % short in 14 of 32).
